title: Dedicated Tenant Network Unreachable — Failover & Escalation Playbook
author: Marcus Chen
body:
Purpose:
This playbook documents the operational steps, automated runbooks, and customer communication templates for responding to a dedicated-tenant networking outage where the tenant's private network or peered connection becomes unreachable. It assumes the customer is on a Dedicated or Private deployment and that Redwood’s control plane is reachable but the tenant's front-line ingress is not.

Scope:
- Applies to Dedicated GPU tenants, Private (VPC) deployments, and on-prem connectors.
- Covers detection, immediate mitigation, automated traffic failover, customer comms, and post-incident verification.
- Does NOT cover full-region cloud provider outages (see Major Cloud Provider Outage playbook).

Owner & Roles:
- Primary owner: Customer Success Engineering (CSE) — incident lead until handoff.
- Networking oncall (NetOps) — responsible for peering/firewall checks and cross-account routing.
- Platform SRE — responsible for routing/proxy changes and slot-level capacity.
- Customer Technical Contact (CTC) — validates reachability and accepts proposed cutover window.

Detection signals (high-confidence indicators):
1) Tenant ingress health: 5xx spikes, consistent 10-second TCP connect timeouts from multiple PoPs.
2) Customer-side alerts: CTC reports inability to reach ingress, or their NOC ticket opened.
3) Observability: Missing request traces with tenant tag, connection reset counters on ingress, BGP/peering flaps (if available).
4) Telemetry: Sudden drop in token throughput for tenant > 2 minutes while upstream control-plane heartbeats continue.

Pre-run checks (do before any manual failover):
- Confirm control plane reachable: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/<tenant-id>/health 
- Verify that Dedicated proxy (edge) is accepting health checks from other tenants.
- Check capacity headroom on candidate fallback pools (Dedicated pool or shared Hosted fallback): current_gpu_utilization < 75% and queued_requests < 1000.
- Ensure customer has signed failover SLA in contract (if required).

Immediate mitigation (fast, reversible actions):
1) Notify CTC: use template in section "Customer Communication Templates — Initial Notification".
2) Temporarily increase ingress retry/backoff for the tenant to allow short network blips: update config in config-store: 
   curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://controlplane.redwood.ai/api/v1/tenants/<tenant-id>/ingress-config -d '{"retries":5, "backoff_ms":2000}'
3) If the tenant uses a dedicated inbound IP (peered), ask NetOps to run a quick traceroute and check peering metrics: traceroute -n <tenant-ingress-ip> from two PoPs.
4) Open a severity-level incident in PagerDuty and Slack #prod-tenant-incidents. Tag: tenant:<tenant-id> network:unreachable

Automated failover procedure (when automatic fallback is enabled):
- Conditions to trigger automation (AND):
  * control-plane healthy for > 60s
  * tenant ingress failing from >= 3 PoPs for >= 120s
  * candidate fallback pool capacity >= required_slots_by_tenant
- Automation steps (implemented as an orchestration job with idempotency):
  1) Snapshot current routing and KV cache pointers for tenant. Save to incident-runbook: 
     POST https://controlplane.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents/<incident-id>/artifacts -d '{"snapshot_type":"routing","payload":{...}}'
  2) Scale-up warm replicas in fallback pool to required_slots_by_tenant + 20% buffer.
  3) Activate traffic-splitting: route 10% -> fallback, 90% -> primary for 5 minutes, then 100% -> fallback if metrics are stable.
  4) Apply per-tenant token limits & cost-protections (throttle <= 2x baseline QPS) while on fallback.
  5) Keep KV cache in read-only mode for 10 minutes; begin cold-warm cache warming using historically requested keys.
  6) Notify CTC of failover completion and expected behavior differences.

Manual emergency failover (operator steps):
1) Confirm approvals: Incident lead + SRE engineering manager (Slack + ASAP).
2) Run: 
   a) Set tenant routing override: 
      curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://controlplane.redwood.ai/api/v1/tenants/<tenant-id>/override-routing -d '{"target_pool":"fallback-pool-3","reason":"network-unreachable","operator":"<your-email>"}'
   b) Validate: curl https://controlplane.redwood.ai/api/v1/tenants/<tenant-id>/status | jq '.routing'
   c) Scale fallback: terraform apply -var='tenant_slots=<n>' modules/fallback-pool 
3) If traffic is stuck in transit, issue a soft-reset on connection broker: systemctl restart redwood-connector-broker && monitor logs: journalctl -u redwood-connector-broker -f --since "5m"

Customer communication templates:
- Initial Notification (within 5 minutes):
  Subject: Redwood — Investigating connectivity to your dedicated tenant (tenant: <tenant-id>)
  Body: "We are investigating reports that your dedicated tenant ingress is unreachable from our points of presence. Our control plane remains healthy. We are running diagnostics (traceroute/BGP checks) and will update within 15 minutes. If you have any network changes in progress, please reply to this thread. Incident ID: <incident-id>."

- Failover Complete (when traffic shifted):
  Subject: Redwood — Traffic shifted to fallback pool for tenant <tenant-id>
  Body: "We have temporarily shifted your traffic to a fallback compute pool to restore service while your network is unreachable. You may observe increased latency (expected +80–200ms) and partial cache cold starts. We have applied cost-protections and request limits to maintain stability. We will keep this in place until you confirm network restoration or we validate recovery. Metrics & logs: <link-to-incident-dashboard>."

- Rollback Confirmation (after primary network restored):
  Subject: Redwood — Confirming rollback to primary ingress for tenant <tenant-id>
  Body: "We observed successful reachability checks to your primary ingress and will initiate a controlled rollback. Expected effects: brief re-warm of caches and sub-second routing handoff. Please confirm if you prefer a maintenance window for rollback. Incident ID: <incident-id>."

Escalation matrix (contact and target response times):
| Role | Primary contact | PagerDuty | Target response |
|-----|-----------------|----------:|----------------:|
| CSE Incident Lead | Marcus Chen | PD:CS-CSE-Network | 5 min |
| Networking Oncall | NetOps Team | PD:NetOps | 10 min |
| Platform SRE | SRE Duty | PD:SRE-Platform | 10 min |
| Engineering Manager | Leah Gomez | PD:EngMgr | 30 min |
| Customer Success Director | Omar Siddiqui | PD:CSD | 60 min |

Verification & Recovery tests (post-failover):
- Validate request success rate > 99% for 10 minutes from three regions. Query: SELECT success_rate FROM telemetry.tenant_http WHERE tenant_id='<tenant-id>' AND window='10m';
- End-to-end trace check: ensure new traces contain fallback-pool identifiers and no connection resets.
- KV cache hit-rate should steadily improve > 50% within 20 minutes of traffic shift.

Post-incident RCA checklist (owner: Incident lead):
1) Collect diagnostic artifacts: traceroutes, peering logs, BGP state, control-plane routing snapshots, and fallback pool scaling events.
2) Time-series: token throughput, 5xxs, connection resets annotated with timeline.
3) Cost impact estimate and applied cost-protections.
4) Root cause hypothesis and required long-term mitigations (e.g., additional peering, multi-region ingress, improved health check logic).
5) Publish RCA to customer and internal stakeholders within 72 hours.

Runbook tuning & automated tests:
- Monthly chaos test: simulate tenant ingress blackhole in staging and validate automated failover completes in <5 minutes.
- Quarterly capacity rehearsal: ensure candidate fallback pools have > 25% spare capacity margin for peak tenants.
- Add telemetry alerts: new rule 'tenant_ingress_unreachable_v2' triggers when loss_of_connectivity_ratio > 0.8 across 3 PoPs for 120s.

Operational notes & pitfalls:
- Avoid immediate rollback on transient flaps; prefer 5–15 minute observation windows.
- KV cache is largely ephemeral when failing over. Customers with strict consistency may see variance — pre-authorized read-only policies reduce user-facing errors.
- Always verify that IP-based ACLs on customer side are not the root cause before scaling fallback pools.

Appendix: useful commands & dashboards
- Check tenant routing: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane.redwood.ai/api/v1/tenants/<tenant-id>/routing | jq
- Traceroute from PoP: ssh pop-1.redwood.ai -- traceroute -n <tenant-ip>
- Kibana query (requests): tenant_id:"<tenant-id>" AND response_code:[500 TO 599] | date_histogram(1m)
- Incident dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/<incident-id>/tenant-failover
